sections.heading: Overview
bullets: Mei Tanaka led a blameless review of Tuesday's 52-minute route optimizer outage, during which dispatchers could see empty routes and 31 customer accounts had at least one affected request.
The group separated confirmed route-generation failures from unverified delivery outcomes and kept the index change rolled back pending further evidence.

sections.heading: Key points
bullets: Lucas Ferreira said a changed database index altered the nightly job's query plan, and the job held a lock on route-input tables while optimizer requests waited and timed out.
The service translated optimizer timeouts into empty route arrays, so Jonas Weber's board showed a blank state that looked like a legitimate zero-route result.
Lucas placed the first alert about 18 minutes after the first empty result, while a support ticket arrived roughly nine minutes before the page.
Amara Nwosu counted 31 affected accounts from failed requests, but only eleven contacted support, and the team could not confirm delivery impact for every account.
Mei paused the nightly job, Lucas rolled back the index, and the team checked two successful optimizer cycles before treating route generation as stable.
Amara said the status page stayed green after customer reports because no owner or symptom-based declaration trigger had been clear.

sections.heading: Decisions
bullets: Mei and Lucas agreed that timeout-derived route failures should drive the primary page, with lock-wait duration serving as a diagnostic signal and replay data used to tune thresholds.
Mei agreed to return an explicit service error rather than an empty route array, and Jonas will design a route-error state that labels any last good plan with its timestamp.
The incident lead will name a communications owner and decide on a status-page post within ten minutes of confirmed route-generation impact, without waiting for a root-cause diagnosis.
Mei will keep the index change rolled back and treat restarting the nightly job separately from another index deploy.

sections.heading: Open questions
bullets: Lucas has not yet verified whether a bounded replay under the changed index reproduces the lock and would trigger the proposed alert within five minutes.
The team cannot tell from existing logs whether every affected account saw a blank board or whether any particular delivery was missed.

sections.heading: Pain points
bullets: Amara Nwosu said dispatchers saw empty routes during a 52-minute period, and one dispatcher reported that every truck appeared unassigned.
Eleven customers contacted support; one dispatcher used a printed morning route sheet, while another waited to release trucks.
Amara said the status page still showed green after support had customer reports, which made the outage harder to explain.

sections.heading: Current solution
bullets: Mei paused the nightly job and Lucas rolled back the index; support then told callers to refresh after route generation recovered.
Lucas said request logs confirm regenerated routes, but the team cannot prove every open browser tab refreshed automatically.

sections.heading: Objections
bullets: Omar Haddad objected to treating the 31 affected accounts as 31 missed deliveries because the count comes from failed optimizer requests.
Amara objected to promising a permanent fix in customer notes while the index change was only rolled back and controlled validation remained unfinished.

sections.heading: Next steps
bullets: Amara will draft a factual note for the 31 affected accounts by end of week and make a separate call list for the eleven customers who contacted support.
Omar will review Amara's wording about financial impact today without delaying the operational facts.
Amara will prepare status-page templates by tomorrow, and the incident lead will name a communications owner when an incident is declared.

sections.heading: Yesterday
bullets: Amara Nwosu reconciled support tickets and route-request logs, identifying 31 affected accounts and eleven customers who contacted support.
Lucas Ferreira reconstructed how the changed index and the nightly job's long transaction locked route-input tables during Tuesday's outage.

sections.heading: Today
bullets: Mei Tanaka will identify an engineer for the timeout-to-error service change and put incident owners in the tracker today.
Amara Nwosu will send Omar Haddad the draft customer note today and prepare status-page templates by tomorrow.
Omar Haddad will review the customer note today, especially any claim about financial impact.
Lucas Ferreira will prepare a bounded replay and an alert proposal by Friday before the team considers redeploying the changed index.
Jonas Weber will draft a route-error state by next week and then test its wording with two dispatchers alongside Amara Nwosu.

sections.heading: Blockers
bullets: Lucas Ferreira cannot treat the changed index as safe until the production-sized replay tests its interaction with the nightly job.
Jonas Weber needs an explicit optimizer error from Mei Tanaka's service change before the board can reliably distinguish unavailable routes from zero routes.
Amara Nwosu cannot describe a permanent fix or verified delivery outcome in customer communication because the team has only confirmed route restoration.

sections.heading: Goals
bullets: Mei Tanaka wants a deploy review that tests index changes against scheduled jobs and names a rollback owner.
Lucas Ferreira wants customer-visible route-failure alerts to catch an incident like Tuesday's within five minutes.
Amara Nwosu wants a status-page decision within ten minutes of confirmed route-generation impact.

sections.heading: Progress
bullets: Mei paused the nightly job and Lucas rolled back the index; two successful optimizer cycles supported the decision to declare route generation stable.
Amara reconciled logs and tickets to identify 31 affected accounts and eleven customers who contacted support.

sections.heading: Risks
bullets: The nightly job is paused, and Lucas has not yet proved that a full run and the changed index can coexist without locking route-input tables.
The service currently converts optimizer timeouts into empty routes, leaving dispatchers with a misleading blank board.
Server-health alerts fired roughly 18 minutes after the first empty result, and the status page remained green while customers contacted support.
The logs do not establish which of the 31 affected accounts saw a blank board or lost a delivery.

sections.heading: Decisions
bullets: Mei and Lucas chose timeout-derived route failures as the primary paging signal and lock-wait duration as a diagnostic signal.
Mei will keep the index rolled back until the replay and evidence review, while handling the nightly job restart as a separate decision.
The incident lead will name a communications owner and make a status-page decision within ten minutes of confirmed impact.

sections.heading: Next steps
bullets: Mei will publish the revised deploy checklist by Friday and identify the engineer for the timeout-to-error service change today.
Lucas will bring alert thresholds and replay evidence by Friday, including whether the alert would have paged within five minutes on Tuesday.
Jonas will draft a route-error state by next week, and Amara will test its wording with two dispatchers.
Amara will draft status-page templates by tomorrow and a factual customer note by end of week, with Omar reviewing financial-impact language today.
Mei will hold an evidence review next week covering the replay, alert path, status update exercise, and board error state.
